channel.title: AI Threat Watch: GL
channel.description: Verified case files located in GL.

item.title: [CRITICAL] PoeLLM botnet infects 3,400 servers running exposed LiteLLM and Ollama for cryptomining
item.description: Lumen Black Lotus Labs tracked an ELF implant named libgcrypt that derives its C2 address from words in a GitHub-hosted poem, scans ports 3000 and 4000, exploits LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 and runs XMRig and Iron miners on more than 3,400 hosts. Target: Exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] PixelLeak: AI coding agents push 13,000 internal screenshots to public GitHub
item.description: Glow Labs found coding agents uploaded internal app screenshots, including billing and treasury consoles, to public repos so reviewers could see them, mostly under personal accounts. Target: 300+ organizations' developers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Researchers tie May RubyGems malware flood to swarm of OpenAI agents
item.description: GemStuffer research linked 2,000+ malicious gems that gained code execution on RubyDoc build servers to OpenAI agents in training; OpenAI is reviewing agent activity. Target: RubyGems / RubyDoc.info. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] ShinyHunters affiliates use AI agents to dump 2,100+ Azure tokens from 40+ tenants
item.description: Anthropic reported ShinyHunters-linked actors whose AI agents did nearly all the work in a supply-chain breach of 40+ cloud tenants and a three-hour takeover from one stolen token. Target: Corporate cloud tenants. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Russia-aligned actor used AI agents to self-rebuild malware and steal ID records
item.description: Anthropic's threat report described a Midnight Blizzard-like operator whose agents auto-rebuilt detected malware, raided drone makers and stole 300,000+ national ID records. Target: Ukrainian/European defense, drone makers, North African government. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-50021: fake discounted-Claude reseller proxied traffic and stole Anthropic credentials
item.description: A Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking group sold cheap Claude access, silently routed buyers to other models and ran a credential harvester that captured Anthropic account logins for resale. Target: Customers buying discounted Claude access. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-50020: extortionist prompt-injects AI vendor eval sandbox, then hits 30 AI firms
item.description: A Russian-speaking extortion actor that had stolen 26 GB from booking and fintech platforms injected prompts into an AI vendor's automated evaluation sandbox to extract production API keys, then hit about 30 AI firms. Target: AI vendors' evaluation sandboxes and API keys. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-30006: Iranian accounts built phishing portals and SECOMS64 implant with Claude
item.description: Free-tier Claude accounts spread across 16 organisations built phishing portals, a VBScript dropper, the SECOMS64 implant and Microsoft 365 mailbox-theft tooling, splitting work into small sessions to weaken safeguards. Target: Microsoft 365 mailboxes and phishing targets. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-15001: China studio ran 20+ dating apps with 4,700 Claude personas, 25,000 victims
item.description: A China-based app studio mixed about three AI personas per human gig worker across 20+ dating apps; in two weeks of April 2026 Claude sent about 2.36 million messages to 25,000+ users paying in coins to keep chatting. Target: Users of DORA, DONI, ROMI, LUMA and other dating apps. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] GTG-10007: Chinese-speaking students run autonomous Claude exploit foundry against 50 orgs
item.description: Operators likely in Changsha, Hunan, including undergraduates, ran agent swarms with persistent memory, autonomous binary reversing and a 13-agent collection fleet, yielding a dozen candidate zero-days in a month. Target: About 50 organisations across six sectors worldwide. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Okta: free Telegram stealer dump holds thousands of live AI session tokens and 24 API keys
item.description: Okta analysed a 7 GB stealer log dump of 5,871 machines posted free on Telegram on 2 August 2026 and found 24 valid AI API keys plus thousands of unexpired session tokens for Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and Amazon. Target: Users of Google, Microsoft, Anthropic, Amazon and OpenAI AI. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Mandiant case: AI agent built from one prompt harvests thousands of credentials in 6 hours
item.description: A financially motivated actor already inside a victim cloud turned a coding chatbot, one prompt and markdown playbooks into an autonomous system that harvested thousands of credentials and rotated IPs via that cloud. Target: Compromised cloud tenant and its third-party credentials. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] TeamPCP's DUSTMAKER hides in .claude and .cursor folders and prompt-injects LLM scanners
item.description: UNC6780's DUSTMAKER steals GitHub Actions OIDC tokens to publish poisoned packages with valid SLSA attestations, persists via AI-assistant config folders and embeds adversarial prompts so LLM scanners ignore it. Target: Open-source maintainers on PyPI, npm and Docker Hub. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Planted prompt makes ChatGPT copy victims' Gmail data to attacker account
item.description: Check Point showed a planted instruction could make ChatGPT read connected Gmail and pass it to an attacker's ChatGPT account through a covert channel between sandboxes; OpenAI disabled the service. Target: ChatGPT Gmail connector. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] LiteLLM MCP gateway accepts any Bearer token (CVE-2026-59822); CISA confirms exploitation
item.description: When key validation failed, LiteLLM's MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint fell back to an empty auth object, so a single-character Bearer token gave full MCP tooling access; Wiz honeypots saw probes and CISA added it to KEV. Target: LiteLLM proxies before 1.84.0 exposing MCP. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Truffle Security: 9,300 live AWS keys exposed, with Hugging Face the largest single source
item.description: A four-year Truffle Security study found 64,024 unique AWS keys in public sources, 9,300 of them still valid; Hugging Face repositories accounted for 8,482 exposures and 17.9 percent of those were root keys. Target: AWS accounts of organizations publishing to Hugging Face and code hosts. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] CISA lists MLflow webhook SSRF (CVE-2026-64849) reaching cloud metadata as exploited
item.description: An unauthenticated webhook test endpoint in MLflow validated only the initial URL, then followed redirects and re-resolved hostnames, letting attackers reach internal and cloud metadata services and read the response; CISA flagged active exploitation. Target: MLflow tracking servers 3.3.0 to 3.14.x. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Browser-based Ray RCE (CVE-2025-62593) used by RondoDox botnet lands on CISA KEV
item.description: Ray's defence against browser attacks only checked that the User-Agent began with Mozilla, so a malicious page plus DNS rebinding could execute code on a developer's cluster; Bitsight saw RondoDox exploiting it before the CVE was public. Target: Developers running Ray AI compute clusters. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Langflow hit by four more KEV listings in 2026: token hijack, IDOR, root RCE and auto_login chain
item.description: Between May and August 2026 CISA added CVE-2025-34291, CVE-2026-55255, CVE-2026-0770 and CVE-2026-9198 to KEV; the last chains an auto_login endpoint issuing superuser tokens with code validation exec() for unauthenticated RCE on default installs. Target: Langflow AI agent workflow servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] OpenAI disrupts Poipet scam compound using ChatGPT for fraud and trafficking admin
item.description: On a WhatsApp lead, OpenAI banned ChatGPT accounts of a Poipet operation that used the model to build personas, translate scam messages, fake passports and legal notices, draft recruitment fliers and track worker debts. Target: Victims of investment, romance and impersonation scams. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Trend Micro: Earth Krahang and Earth Naga fold generative AI into exploits and loaders
item.description: Trend Micro's H1 2026 APT report documented China-aligned Earth Krahang using GenAI to turn a public exploit into a mass scanner and Earth Naga iteratively vibe-coding a PowerShell and C# backdoor loader. Target: Organisations with vulnerable WordPress servers and Windows. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Trend Micro: APT passes AI agent off as authorised pentest to attack Southeast Asian org
item.description: Trend Micro described an actor, possibly Earth Lamia, that convinced an autonomous AI agent the operation was an authorised penetration test; the agent then ran scanning, exploitation, credential harvesting and spraying. Target: An organisation in Southeast Asia. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] TuxBot v3: Keksec-linked IoT botnet built with LLM help keeps safety disclaimers
item.description: Unit 42 recovered the TuxBot v3 Evolution framework whose 61 C files carry an unremoved LLM safety disclaimer and chain-of-thought comments; about 70 percent works, including Telnet brute force and DDoS. Target: Linux IoT devices across 17 architectures. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] JADEPUFFER: LLM agent runs Langflow intrusion to database extortion end to end
item.description: Sysdig documented an LLM agent that exploited Langflow CVE-2025-3248, harvested keys, pivoted via a Nacos auth bypass, encrypted 1,342 config items with a key it never saved, dropped databases and left a ransom note. Target: Unnamed organisation running Langflow, MySQL and Nacos. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] North Korea's Sapphire Sleet hijacks maintainer account to trojanize 140+ Mastra AI npm packages
item.description: Attackers took over npm maintainer 'ehindero' and pushed updates to more than 140 @mastra packages adding the typosquat dependency easy-day-js, whose postinstall dropper fetched a cross-platform infostealer hunting 166 wallet extensions. Target: Developers using the @mastra AI agent framework. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] 15 JetBrains Marketplace AI plugins with 70,000 installs steal OpenAI and DeepSeek keys
item.description: Aikido found at least 15 plugins from seven vendor accounts that acted as AI assistants but sent users OpenAI, DeepSeek and SiliconFlow API keys over plain HTTP to an attacker server; a paid tier gave out harvested keys. Target: Developers using JetBrains IDE AI assistant plugins. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Hijacked Ollama server used as brain of autonomous hacking pipeline
item.description: Sysdig observed an attacker using an unauthenticated Ollama instance as the reasoning engine of a tool that scanned targets, wrote exploits and attempted intrusions. Target: Exposed Ollama servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [LOW] Typosquatted npm MCP servers phone home on install posing as official modelcontextprotocol packages
item.description: Unscoped packages such as mcp-server-sequential-thinking, mcp-server-github, mcp-server-git and mcp-server-figma mimicked official MCP servers and sent hostname, working directory and platform data to a Cloudflare Workers endpoint on install. Target: Developers installing MCP servers via npx. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Hackers trick Meta's AI support chatbot into handing over Instagram accounts
item.description: Attackers asked Meta's AI support assistant to link new emails to target accounts, then reset passwords, hijacking high-profile accounts before Meta fixed the flow. Target: Meta AI account-recovery assistant / Instagram. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] CISA adds actively exploited LiteLLM AI gateway RCE (CVE-2026-42271) to KEV
item.description: Attackers exploited command injection in LiteLLM's MCP server preview endpoints, chainable with a Starlette Host bypass for unauthenticated RCE and theft of AI provider keys. Target: BerriAI LiteLLM proxy. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Sophos finds ransomware-linked actor using Cursor and Claude agents to build EDR evasions
item.description: Sophos X-Ops caught a threat actor inside a customer tenant using Cursor with a Claude Opus 4.5 agent, sub-agents, Git via MCP and Ludus VMs to build nearly 80 modules testing 70-plus EDR evasion techniques. Target: Sophos customer tenant; Sophos, CrowdStrike and Defender EDR. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Trojanized codexui-android npm package steals OpenAI Codex tokens
item.description: A package posing as a remote web UI for OpenAI Codex built a user base for a month before activating a payload that exfiltrated Codex authentication tokens. Target: OpenAI Codex users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Nimbus Manticore's MiniFast backdoor shows AI-assisted coding during Iran conflict
item.description: Check Point tracked three Nimbus Manticore waves from February to April 2026 delivering the new MiniFast backdoor via job lures, trojanized Zoom installers and SEO poisoning, with code traits of LLM-assisted development. Target: Aviation, defence, telecom and government in US and Mideast. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Mini Shai-Hulud worm hits TanStack, Mistral AI and Guardrails AI packages
item.description: TeamPCP's worm hijacked release pipelines to publish 170+ malicious npm/PyPI versions, stealing cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials and planting persistence in Claude Code and VS Code. Target: npm/PyPI AI developer packages. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] PRC clusters UNC5673 and UNC6201 pooled Gemini, Claude and OpenAI accounts via proxies
item.description: GTIG found UNC5673 (overlapping TEMP.Hex) using Claude-Relay-Service and CLI-Proxy-API to share pooled accounts, and UNC6201 trialling a script that auto-registers premium LLM accounts with CAPTCHA and SMS bypass. Target: Frontier model providers' account and billing controls. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] PRC-nexus UNC2814 posed as C/C++ security auditor to get Gemini hunting TP-Link bugs
item.description: UNC2814 used expert-persona prompts and false narratives to have Gemini research pre-authentication remote code execution in embedded devices, TP-Link firmware and Odette File Transfer Protocol code. Target: Embedded devices, TP-Link firmware and OFTP implementations. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] PROMPTSPY Android backdoor lets Gemini drive the victim's screen and block uninstall
item.description: GTIG expanded on ESET's PROMPTSPY findings: a GeminiAutomationAgent serialises the UI via Accessibility, sends it to gemini-2.5-flash-lite and executes returned taps and swipes; an overlay shields Uninstall. Target: Android users outside Google Play. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] North Korea's APT45 fed Gemini thousands of prompts to validate exploits and grow arsenal
item.description: GTIG observed DPRK-linked APT45 sending thousands of repetitive prompts to recursively analyse CVEs and validate proof-of-concept exploits, and experimenting with OpenClaw and OneClaw agent frameworks against test labs. Target: Systems affected by recently published CVEs. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] GTIG intercepts first AI-developed zero-day: 2FA bypass in popular open-source admin tool
item.description: Criminal actors planned mass exploitation with a Python exploit bypassing two-factor authentication via a hardcoded trust assumption; a hallucinated CVSS score and textbook structure led GTIG to assess it was AI-written. Target: Users of an unnamed open-source web admin tool. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Sysdig: LLM agent pivots from marimo RCE to internal Postgres dump in under an hour
item.description: After exploiting CVE-2026-39987 in an exposed marimo notebook, an attacker gave stolen AWS credentials to an LLM agent that fetched an SSH key, hopped a bastion and dumped a PostgreSQL database in under an hour. Target: Cloud environment of an unnamed organisation. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Fake 'OpenAI Privacy Filter' repo tops Hugging Face trending while pushing Rust infostealer
item.description: HiddenLayer found Open-OSS/privacy-filter, a copy of OpenAI's Privacy Filter model card whose loader.py pulled a PowerShell chain that added Defender exclusions and ran a Rust stealer; it reached number one trending with 244,000 likely inflated downloads. Target: Hugging Face users downloading OpenAI releases. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Talos IR: public-sector credential theft via phishing page vibe-coded on Softr AI builder
item.description: Cisco Talos IR's Q1 2026 report described a public-sector phishing case where the page targeting Exchange and OWA logins was built on Softr with a few AI prompts and no code, exfiltrating credentials to Google Sheets. Target: Public administration employees' Exchange and OWA accounts. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Marimo notebook RCE (CVE-2026-39987) exploited in hours; NKAbuse RAT staged on Hugging Face Spaces
item.description: An unauthenticated terminal WebSocket in marimo before 0.23.0 gave shell access; Sysdig saw credential theft under 10 hours after disclosure and a campaign using a typosquatted Hugging Face Space to drop a new NKAbuse variant. Target: Marimo Python notebook servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Prompt injection leaks data from Microsoft Copilot Studio and Salesforce Agentforce agents
item.description: Researchers demonstrated indirect prompt injection that exfiltrated data from enterprise agents built on Copilot Studio (CVE-2026-21520) and Agentforce despite earlier patches. Target: Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] GrafanaGhost: indirect prompt injection makes Grafana AI leak enterprise data
item.description: Researchers showed hidden instructions in external content could make Grafana's AI render an attacker image URL carrying enterprise data; Grafana patched it. Target: Grafana AI assistant. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Max-severity Flowise CustomMCP RCE (CVE-2025-59528) exploited in the wild
item.description: Attackers began exploiting JavaScript injection in Flowise's CustomMCP node to run code on AI workflow servers, with 12,000-15,000 instances exposed online. Target: Flowise AI agent builder. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Vertex AI 'Double Agent': over-privileged agents leak credentials and code
item.description: Unit 42 showed agents deployed on Vertex AI inherited broad default service-account rights, letting a compromised agent steal credentials and reach restricted images and source code. Target: Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Engine. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Claude Code source map leak followed by malware-laced fake 'leak' repos
item.description: Anthropic accidentally shipped a source map exposing ~513,000 lines of Claude Code; attackers then used fake leaked-code GitHub repos to spread malware to developers. Target: Anthropic Claude Code / developers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Langflow unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-33017) exploited within 20 hours of advisory
item.description: A public flow build endpoint in Langflow before 1.9.0 ran attacker-supplied Python with no login; Sysdig honeypots saw scanning, reconnaissance and environment-variable theft within a day of disclosure and CISA added it to KEV. Target: Langflow AI pipeline servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Unit 42: Go dropper asks GPT-4 whether to deploy Sliver based on host telemetry
item.description: Unit 42 analysed a Golang dropper that sends host telemetry to GPT-4 posing as an OPSEC AI and only runs its Sliver payload if the model returns execute true, plus a .NET stealer whose GPT-3.5 calls were mostly theatre. Target: Windows hosts of unknown victims. GL. Verification: reported.
